clauses.reason: A Signetum-owned entry switch and version storage conflict with host plugin managers, and a standalone Skill cannot carry a command hook.

updates.rationale: Both hosts replace a plugin's versioned cache directory on update and Codex deletes the old one at once, so a Signetum-managed entry switch would point a host at content it did not install. Running the host commands after the compatibility check keeps one path that cannot skip a host; printing them would leave each upgrade to manual commands. Pinning the release commit in marketplace.json keeps ordinary merges to main from becoming releases.
updates.statement: Manifest format stays 5. Omitted evidence fields mean the published evidence protocol and schema digest, and an explicit digest must equal that schema. update reads the released marketplace pin on the delivery branch, verifies the pinned Skill against its release metadata, prepares that candidate's environment and checks the project manifest, then upgrades every host that has signetum@signetum installed through its own plugin manager and preserves a Codex user setting that disabled it. An equal Skill digest or an older pin changes nothing, an incompatible manifest returns migration_required before any host command, and --check stays read-only. There is no other install or update path: no standalone Skill install, --to, --source, version storage or entry switch. The updater never edits the project. Skill content identity and engine implementation identity stay separate and share one labeled digest function.

updates.rationale: Codex reads the Claude manifest, marketplace and hooks files and sets CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT, so one tree serves both hosts; a hook can only ship inside a plugin, and the Skill stays the single instruction and execution entry inside it.
updates.statement: Signetum is distributed as the signetum plugin for Claude Code and Codex from one tree, plugins/signetum, carrying the standard signetum Skill (loaded as signetum:signetum) and the command guard. New and existing projects share one explicit local adoption path. Internal scaffold materials are not a second public product.

updates.rationale: The host plugin manager is the installation path users already have, and it carries the guard that a copied Skill folder cannot.
updates.statement: Keep installation, distribution and use simple through one plugin installed by each host's plugin manager, carrying the standard Skill, and repository-owned instructions and commands. Position for reliable development with large agent teams using concrete cases and accurately bounded evidence.

clauses.reason: Record where the engine environment lives, what the guard refuses, where it applies and how adoption enables it before implementation.

updates.rationale: Codex trusts a plugin hook by hashing the plugin directory and excludes only bytecode, virtual environments and egg-info; a receipt written into the Skill marked the hook modified and the host-python symlink made the plugin unhashable. A path-independent fingerprint also lets the Claude copy, the Codex copy and an update candidate share one prepared environment across host version directories.
updates.statement: The locked engine environment lives in ${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/signetum/runtime/<fingerprint>, where the fingerprint covers the implementation digest, uv.lock and pyproject.toml and not the install path. A shared runtime/host-python link only starts the launcher, which verifies the environment for its own fingerprint. setup and ordinary commands write nothing into the plugin directory except interpreter bytecode caches.

updates.rationale: These are the operations that lost work or bypassed workspace-sync, batch admission, cleanup and workspace-open in Perdura and Signetum. Token-level parsing fixes the regex guard's misses on git -C and --force-with-lease and its false positives on quoted mentions. git commit stays allowed because the protocol commits through it.
updates.statement: The guard reads tool_input.command from Claude Code and Codex Bash payloads and the payload cwd, splits the command into simple commands through quotes, operators, newlines, heredocs, command substitution, sh -c, eval and common wrappers, and skips Git global options. It exits 2 with one JSON line naming the category and the Signetum operation to use for stash other than list or show, reset --hard, restore other than --staged alone, clean other than a dry run, checkout -- or ., forced checkout, forced or discarding switch, forced push or +refspec, recursive forced rm of ., *, ~, / or $HOME, any git merge or rebase, wt step rebase or push, wt merge, git worktree add, move or remove, wt remove, wt switch -c or --create, git branch -D or --delete --force, and pre-commit run while git diff reports unstaged changes. Other commands, including read-only Git, git commit and git branch -d, exit 0.

updates.rationale: Enable scope is already a host-owned choice, so a second switch would only duplicate it. Failing open matches both hosts, which block only on exit 2, and keeps a broken guard from stopping every shell command; the owner accepted that trade.
updates.statement: The guard has no internal repository switch: wherever the plugin is enabled the whole rule set applies. A missing interpreter, malformed payload, exception or timeout exits 0 with a diagnostic, and the sh entry maps every status other than 2 to 0.

updates.rationale: Project settings are committed with the repository, so every collaborator's host enables the guard there, and the guard's scope follows the repositories that adopted the protocol. Codex merges trusted project config layers into the plugin set, verified with codex-cli 0.166.0 in a temporary home.
updates.statement: The adoption preview that writes signetum.toml also enables the plugin at project scope: enabledPlugins signetum@signetum and the signetum GitHub marketplace in .claude/settings.json, and [plugins."signetum@signetum"] enabled = true in .codex/config.toml. Other settings are preserved, enabled files stay unchanged and an explicit disable is refused for review. Codex reads that layer only for trusted projects and only for a plugin installed in the user's Codex home.

decisions.reason: The owner approved one plugin with a command guard, host-managed installation and updates, project-scope enablement through adoption and a runtime outside the plugin directory.

boundaries: One manifest format and one published evidence schema digest.
Host plugin managers own installed copies; Signetum never rewrites them.
The plugin directory receives no generated runtime files.
revision.summary: One host-managed plugin carries the Skill and its command guard; the engine environment lives outside it.

boundaries: The guard applies wherever the plugin is enabled; it has no repository switch.
A guard that cannot run allows the command.
revision.summary: A plugin PreToolUse guard refuses commands that lose work or bypass protocol operations.

transaction.reason: Apply the owner-approved plugin distribution, runtime, guard and project enablement rules before implementation

observations.reason: In a temporary CODEX_HOME with codex-cli 0.166.0, re-running codex plugin add on a plugin whose user setting was enabled = false set it back to true, so an update through the Codex plugin manager would silently widen a project-only guard to every repository. With the user setting false and a trusted project's .codex/config.toml enabling signetum@signetum, app-server hooks/list and skills/list returned the guard and signetum:signetum only for that project; an untrusted project layer is ignored (config loader tests). marketplace upgrade refuses a local marketplace.
observations.summary: codex plugin add rewrites the user setting to enabled = true, and Codex merges a trusted project's .codex/config.toml into the plugin set.

observations.reason: claude --plugin-dir plugins/signetum -p (2.1.318, session only, in a scratch git clone --shared with a dirty file) ran git status, then had git stash refused with category stash from the signetum@inline plugin; the file stayed modified and no stash entry was created. Its init listed signetum:signetum next to the old standalone signetum entry, confirming the duplicate the migration note removes. In a temporary CODEX_HOME without credentials and a scratch local marketplace, codex plugin add installed 0.3.3; app-server hooks/list showed /bin/sh <cache>/skills/signetum/scripts/command-guard and skills/list showed signetum:signetum. After recording the reviewed hash, sh <cache>/skills/signetum/scripts/signetum setup, identity and status ran with a temporary XDG_DATA_HOME, no file in the cache changed and hooks/list still reported the hook trusted.
observations.summary: Real host probes: Claude Code refused a sentinel stash through the plugin hook and listed signetum:signetum; Codex listed the expanded hook and skill, and the hook stayed trusted after setup and commands from its cache copy.
